_why: Cases where the engine contradicts the fixture author. Reviewed by hand, never generated blind: the expectations predate the port and nothing shows the suite was ever green, so a disagreement may be an engine bug OR a fixture that was always wrong. Categories: browser (Firefox → Chromium), events (nsIEventListenerService is not reproducible), network (needs a real domain or DNS), fixture (the expectation is wrong), engine (a real defect), unclassified (not yet looked at). The count is a floor: it may shrink, never silently grow. An entry may carry `badReference`: the fixture points at a file whose spelling does not match the one on disk, so it 404s under the case-exact server. Where that coexists with another cause, both are recorded — picking one would misinform.

The call throws, the catch returns false, and false is `i`. Firefox-only API; nothing to fix in the engine short of rewriting the rule against getPropertyValue().

Fixing the reference would restore a test that has never run as intended — a deliberate change to historical test data, not made here.
